title: Aeroradioactivity maps in heavy-mineral exploration - Charleston, South Carolina, area
citation: Force, E.R., Grosz, A.E., Loferski, P.J., and Maybin, A.H., 1982, Aeroradioactivity maps in heavy-mineral exploration - Charleston, South Carolina, area: U.S. Geological Survey Professional Paper 1218, map scale 1:500,000.
notes: Aeroradioactivity/heavy-mineral report: few stratigraphic values. Units are the report's informal facies terms (beach-complex, bay-complex, old Santee River deposits) plus Santee Limestone, Cooper Formation and Ladson Formation members named from Malde (1959). Observations are table 9 channel samples (location, radioactivity, thickness sampled) whose column headers are garbled in the text layer, so column meanings are flagged inferred; heavy-mineral percentages per sample were not recorded except where the text restates them (EF 54C, EF 56A) and the anomaly A auger table 13. Rows of table 9 with missing latitude (EF 27E, others unlabeled) skipped; tables 2, 11, 12 too garbled to read reliably. Radioactivity tables 1-7 not recorded (no schema field). Non-SC references skipped. Plates (pages 25-26) are OCR map sheets with only the anomaly explanation legible.
